label: Outstanding AfCFTA rules-of-origin annexes for the contested sectors are completed before mid-2027
basis: Rules of origin for the sectors where regional value chains are genuinely contested — autos and textiles above all — require agreement among State Parties, and the negotiation has already run well past its original target without closing those annexes. Reference class: multilateral technical annexes whose economics are zero-sum between members, which close slowly or not at all.
rationale: A MARKER priced well below even money, and logged precisely because it is a negative. The asymmetry is structural: a trade agreement's tariff schedule can run on autopilot while the rules that determine WHICH goods qualify stay open, and the open rules are the binding constraint on actual trade. SOFT part: all of it — this is a negotiation among sovereigns and therefore the discretionary-choice class the engine is worst at, which is exactly why it is stated at 0.35 rather than dressed as an invariant.
market: Without rules of origin, a tariff schedule does not move a single container; this is the gate on the whole AfCFTA trade.

label: NOAA declares an ENSO-neutral or La Nina state for the 2027 northern summer
basis: Scheduled official declaration on a fixed monthly cycle; the base rate of neutral-or-Nina against El Nino across a randomly chosen season favours this side.
rationale: Scheduled EVENT with a base-rate value. The declaration is by a named agency on a fixed calendar, which makes the resolution source unambiguous - the #59 fix.
market: ENSO state is the single biggest exogenous input to the ag complex.

label: Aggregate large-bank NIM falls q/q in at least one of the next two reported quarters
basis: Scheduled reporting; the direction rests on deposit beta after a hike, which is a behavioural aggregate rather than a physical constraint. Capped accordingly.
rationale: Scheduled-print class for the event, mid-probability for the value. Deliberately not bundled with a credit-loss claim — one claim per row (#63).
market: Deposit beta is the channel through which a hike hits lending capacity.

label: T-bills stay above 20% of marketable debt outstanding
basis: Near-arithmetic: the bill stock cannot fall below 20% inside a quarter without a paydown larger than any on record. Composition moves slowly by construction.
rationale: Invariant class. Debt composition is a stock, and a stock cannot jump; the claim is about the speed limit on a balance sheet, not about anyone's intent.
market: A high bill share is what keeps the front end supply-heavy and the RRP drained.

label: Brent front-month trades inside $85-$125 for the whole of Q4
basis: No-view odds from `range_odds.py --spot 98 --lo 85 --hi 125 --days 70 --vol 2.5` = 0.33 (--vol is DAILY PERCENT; 2.5%/day is ~40% annualised, consistent with realised wartime Brent). Priced AT the no-view number with no divergence claimed.
rationale: [9/22 CORRECTION #2 - the first correction was WRONG] On 9/21 this was logged at 0.66 without running range_odds.py at all. On 9/22 it was 'corrected' UP to 0.82 on a run that passed --vol 0.80, and --vol is DAILY PERCENT, not annualised: 0.80%/day is ~13% annualised, roughly a third of what wartime Brent has actually realised (101-109 since 9/9, peak close 108.75). At an honest 2.5%/day (~40% annualised), `range_odds.py --spot 98 --lo 85 --hi 125 --days 70 --vol 2.5` returns NO-VIEW 0.33, with only 0.68 sigma to the lower bound. So the original 0.66 was ALREADY too high, and the 0.82 'fix' moved it further the wrong way. Repriced to 0.35, at the no-view number, with NO divergence claimed - the only dated catalyst in sight (the 9/22 Hormuz reopening report) pushes the LOWER bound, not the upper. A units error inside a correction is exactly the shape of the VIX-lookahead and rolling-window failures: the arithmetic was never wrong, the input was. || Level row, ONE asset, explicit band, wide. Note what it is NOT: a call on whether oil goes up or down. The book is 0-for-8 on that question in this tape.

no_view.note: Spot 103.87 is the repo's own tape (STATE.md 9/20). Vol 2.5%/day ~ 40% annualised, which is what the repo's own 9/9-9/20 Brent record implies (101-109 range, peak close 108.75) - a war-premium crude regime, NOT the 0.8%/day (12.8% annualised) that Brent has never sustained. 65 Q4 sessions.

market: The band is the tradeable object; the direction is not.

label: California statewide snowpack peaks below 110% of average in 2027
basis: Measured on a fixed survey calendar; the base rate of a below-110% peak is comfortably above even across the historical record.
rationale: Scheduled measurement with a base-rate value and a NAMED survey as the resolution source. Naming the survey is the #59 fix: that row was scored against the engine only because nobody had written down which measurement counted.
market: Snowpack is the hydro and agricultural input for the whole western US.

label: PBoC reports gold reserve additions in at least 8 of the next 12 monthly reports
basis: Marker on a monthly published series with a long established run. Persistence, not turn.
rationale: Marker class: the claim is that an observable keeps APPEARING, not that it rises or falls. Cheap to check monthly, which is what lesson 6 asks for. Note this is a persistence row on official-sector behaviour, so its failure mode is a policy change, not a price move.
market: Official-sector buying is the structural bid under the gold row in commodities-metals.

label: Local government special bond quota set above CNY 4 trillion
basis: Base rate off the recent quota path; a discretionary number on a fixed calendar.
rationale: Scheduled. The LGSB quota is the real fiscal impulse and a better row than the headline deficit — noted so the two are not treated as independent.
market: The quota is the actual construction-demand number.

label: Official 2026 population figure shows another y/y decline
basis: Demographic arithmetic: the birth cohort and the death cohort are both largely determined years in advance. A reversal would require a fertility jump with no precedent.
rationale: INVARIANT — pure demographic arithmetic, and one of the few things in this tree that is genuinely close to certain. This is the row class the book scores 0.10 Brier on.
market: Demography is the slow denominator under every China demand row.

label: Core PCE y/y prints inside 2.5-4.0% on every release through Q2 2027
basis: Band on a slow-moving y/y series; the base-effect path is arithmetic and the energy pass-through has a known lag length (13g).
rationale: [9/22 CORRECTION] range_odds.py puts the no-view odds at 1.00 and this row was logged at 0.70, -0.30 off it with no dated catalyst in the basis; re-priced 0.70 -> 0.82 toward the arithmetic. Level with a wide band and an explicit base-effect computation. Note 13g: do not downgrade the pass-through thesis on less than one lag length of tape - that error cost #76.

no_view.note: ASSUMED spot core PCE 3.1% y/y and 2.0%/MONTH relative vol (~0.06pp - a y/y series moves slowly by construction). One period = one monthly release; 9 releases to Q2 2027.

market: Core PCE is the mandate variable; everything else is commentary.

label: At least 20 NATO members report defence spending at or above 2% of GDP for 2026
basis: Budgets for the reporting year are already enacted; this is a count of decisions already taken, reported on a fixed annual cycle.
rationale: INVARIANT: enacted budgets are capital-committed. Contrast with a row about future pledges, which would be rhetoric (doctrine 12.1 / R03).
market: Enacted European defence budgets are the demand under the defense-industrial lane.

label: French presidential first round falls inside the Article 7 twenty-to-thirty-five-day pre-expiry window
basis: CONSTITUTIONAL WINDOW: Article 7 of the Fifth Republic constitution requires the election of the President to be held not fewer than twenty and not more than thirty-five days before the expiry of the incumbent's powers, with the second round fourteen days after the first. The government fixes the actual Sundays by decree inside that bracket, so the window is constitutional arithmetic and the day is executive.
rationale: Deliberately a window row: I am not certain of the decreed 2027 Sundays and will not state one as fact. Article 7 also supplies the two-round interval, which means the resolving date for a presidential contest is mechanically fourteen days after whatever first round is decreed. SOFT part: Article 7 also covers vacancy, in which case the window is recomputed off the vacancy rather than off the term, and the node would need re-dating rather than resolving.
market: A fixed fourteen-day inter-round gap is the cleanest dated OAT and CAC vol structure in Europe.

label: German federal investment spending in the 2027 budget exceeds the 2025 level in nominal terms
basis: Nominal comparison against an already-legislated expansion; the base-effect identity makes this arithmetic rather than a policy forecast.
rationale: Invariant, and an explicit use of doctrine 13d.2 the right way round: a NOMINAL comparison against a legislated baseline is arithmetic. The twice-repeated y/y miss came from doing this backwards.
market: German investment is the only large European fiscal impulse in the window.

label: No GLP-1 product appears on the FDA drug shortage list on 2027-06-30
basis: Marker on a published list. Capacity additions are capital-committed and commissioning; demand growth is the offsetting unknown.
rationale: Marker with a named, published resolution source. Two capital-committed forces in opposition again, so the honest price is mid.
market: Shortage status is the cleanest single read on whether capacity has caught demand.

label: Health care and social assistance is the largest contributor to payroll growth in a majority of months through Q2 2027
basis: Downstream of demographic arithmetic and of a funding stream that is statutory. This has been the dominant contributor for an extended run driven by those two facts.
rationale: Invariant-adjacent persistence, mechanistically downstream of the ageing row. Correlation declared: these are one demographic fact observed twice.
market: Healthcare job growth is why 'the labour market' and 'the cyclical labour market' diverge.

label: IG OAS holds under 160bp through year-end
basis: Reference class: IG OAS has breached 160 only in genuine risk events (2008, 2011, 2016, 2020, 2022 briefly). Unconditional quarterly base rate of a breach is low.
rationale: [9/22 CORRECTION] range_odds.py puts the no-view odds at 0.98 and this row was logged at 0.74, -0.24 off it with no dated catalyst in the basis; re-priced 0.74 -> 0.82 toward the arithmetic. Level row. The credit market is the single best falsifier for every 'regime break' story in this book — if the hike is breaking something, it shows up here first.

no_view.note: ASSUMED spot 110bp IG OAS and 2.0%/day relative OAS vol (no live feed). 70 sessions to 12/31; one-sided because the row only claims the upper bound.

market: IG is the cleanest read on whether the hike is a policy error or a policy success.

label: At least 24 NATO members are reported at or above 2% of GDP for 2026
basis: Enacted budgets for the reporting year; this is a count of decisions already taken, published on a fixed annual cycle.
rationale: Invariant. Correlated with the europe lane's defence row - the same enacted budgets counted against a different threshold. Declared, not double-counted.
market: The count is the demand signal European primes book against.

label: Reported quarterly datacenter revenue at the leading accelerator vendor grows sequentially in at least 3 of the next 4 quarters
basis: Scheduled reporting; growth is supply-capped (see the packaging and HBM rows) rather than demand-capped, which makes the constraint knowable.
rationale: Scheduled with a SUPPLY-side mechanism. Priced at the non-invariant ceiling. The important structural point: when supply is the binding constraint, the forecastable variable is capacity, not demand - and capacity schedules are published.
market: Sequential growth is the number the whole complex trades off.

label: Platinum records a supply deficit for 2026
basis: South African shaft depletion and power constraints cap supply; the constraint is physical and already visible in reported output.
rationale: Invariant. Correlated with the silver row through 'precious industrial deficit' - declared so the book does not treat them as two independent confirmations (#70/#27).
market: PGMs are the most supply-constrained precious complex.

label: 2027 US corporate maturity wall exceeds 2026's
basis: Pure arithmetic. The maturity schedule of already-issued bonds is known today; the only way 2027 comes in under 2026 is a large tender/refi wave, which is observable in advance.
rationale: INVARIANT class, and the highest-P row in the buildout for that reason. P>=0.80 is reserved for exactly this (R13): a fact about paper already printed.
market: The wall is the reason a 4% 10y matters more in 2027 than in 2026.

label: A previously announced refinery closure completes on schedule
basis: Capital already committed: an announced closure is a capital decision taken, and reversal requires fresh capital plus a restart schedule once units are cold. Reference class: announced refinery closures that completed.
rationale: Invariant class: a closure announcement is a committed action, unlike a strike PLAN (#72), which is a negotiating instrument. The distinction between committed and announced-intent is the single most useful line the 16.14 patch drew.
market: Closures are why crack spreads can stay wide with crude flat.

label: A merger that draws a Second Request cannot lawfully close inside thirty days of certifying substantial compliance
basis: STATUTORY WAITING PERIOD: the Hart-Scott-Rodino Act bars consummation during an initial thirty-day waiting period, and a request for additional information extends it so that a further thirty-day period runs from the date the parties certify substantial compliance. The clock is statutory and runs regardless of the agency's view of the deal; only the parties' compliance date, not the length of the period, is variable.
rationale: Pure clock arithmetic and a direct answer to the way merger-arb spreads misprice timing. The node says nothing about whether a deal is challenged, cleared or abandoned — it says the EARLIEST lawful closing date is computable from a certification date. SOFT part: timing agreements routinely extend the period by consent, and pull-and-refile resets the initial period, so the statutory floor is a floor and not an estimate.
market: The floor on closing dates is what sets the carry on every arb position with a Second Request.

label: Immobilisation of Russian central-bank assets still rests on a periodically renewed instrument at mid-2027
basis: LEGAL-INSTRUMENT ARITHMETIC: the immobilisation is not a permanent confiscation — it is a restrictive measure carried by a Council instrument with a stated expiry that must be renewed on the same six-month cycle and by the same unanimity rule as the sectoral package. The claim is about the LEGAL FORM of the measure on a date, which is documentary, not about the policy.
rationale: This is the node that explains why the reparations-loan argument exists at all: an asset held under a renewable measure cannot safely be pledged against a multi-decade liability, and that is a legal-structure fact, not an opinion. SOFT part: the Commission has floated moving the measure to a qualified-majority legal basis, which would change the renewal arithmetic; a PROPOSAL to do so is not an adopted act, which is the #72 distinction exactly.
market: Renewable immobilisation is a different collateral than permanent seizure; the difference is the entire financing argument.

label: The 2027 shunto first-round tally reports average wage gains above 4%
basis: Annual spring wage round with a fixed reporting calendar; recent rounds have cleared 4% but the outcome is a negotiated aggregate.
rationale: Scheduled annual event with a negotiated value - so the EVENT is certain and the number is capped. The shunto is the BoJ's own stated precondition, which makes this row upstream of the hike row rather than independent of it. Declared.
market: Shunto is the wage data the BoJ has said it is waiting for.

label: SOFR prints at least 10bp above IORB on a year-end turn date
basis: Marker class: the year-end turn is a recurring balance-sheet constraint, and the spike is mechanical (dealer balance-sheet limits at the reporting date), not a choice.
rationale: Marker, not direction: the claim is that a specific observable APPEARS, on a date fixed by the regulatory calendar. This is the cleanest invariant-shaped row in the lane.
market: A turn spike is the tell that reserves have stopped being ample.

label: UK 30y gilt yield prints above 6.00% on any close by mid-2027
basis: Marker on a tail event. Priced BELOW the book's average on purpose: a book whose rows all sit between 0.40 and 0.88 has no resolution, and genuine tails must be logged as tails.
rationale: A deliberately LOW-probability row. The 9/20 research found every row stated between 0.40 and 0.88 and small-sample-corrected resolution near zero. You cannot fix that by lowering high rows; you fix it by being willing to say 'probably not' and be right.
market: A gilt event is the fastest route from a fiscal story to a global rates event.

label: FY2028 begins under a continuing resolution rather than with all 12 regular bills enacted
basis: Statutory calendar plus a dominant base rate: the fiscal year begins October 1 by statute and there are 12 regular annual appropriations bills. The reference class since the modern budget process began is overwhelmingly 'at least one CR', with full on-time enactment occurring a handful of times in five decades.
rationale: Scheduled class because the DATE is statutory and only the state of the world on it is unknown; priced high off a base rate rather than off any view about the politics of 2027, which is the distinction the #26 miss was bought with. SOFT part: a full-year omnibus enacted in September would resolve this MISS, and the row does not distinguish a CR from a shutdown - a lapse with no CR at all should also resolve HIT on the 'not all 12 enacted' leg, and the label is written to carry that.
market: A CR start caps discretionary outlays at prior-year rates, which is a small but real Q4 fiscal drag.

label: Average hourly earnings y/y prints inside 3.0-5.0% on every release through Q2 2027
basis: Wide band on a slow-moving y/y series; month-to-month movement outside a 200bp band is rare absent a definitional change.
rationale: Level with a wide band on a y/y series - and the base-effect identity check (13d.2) applies: the y/y path has a known arithmetic component from the comparison base.

no_view.note: ASSUMED spot AHE 3.9% y/y and 2.5%/MONTH relative vol (~0.1pp). 9 monthly releases to Q2 2027.

market: Wages inside the band means the energy shock has not become a wage-price process.
